questions.q: What did Yahweh do after David waited patiently for him?
questions.a: Yahweh listened to David and heard his cry.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for David?
questions.a: Yahweh rescued David from the terrible things that had been happening to him as if he’d been in a pit of mud but was lifted out onto a safe and solid rock.

questions.q: What will many do because God has put a new song in David’s mouth?
questions.a: Many will see it and honor him and will trust in Yahweh.
The man is blessed who makes Yahweh his trust and does not honor the proud or those who turn away from Yahweh to lies.

questions.q: How does David describe God’s deeds and thoughts?
questions.a: God’s wonderful deeds are many and his thoughts about us cannot be numbered.

questions.q: What is written about David in the scroll of God’s law?
questions.a: It is written that he delights to do God’s will and that he deeply treasures God’s laws.

questions.q: What has David proclaimed in the great assembly?
questions.a: He has proclaimed good news of God’s righteousness in the great assembly.
He has not concealed God’s righteousness in his heart nor God’s covenant faithfulness nor trustworthiness from the great assembly.

questions.q: What does David pray that Yahweh will do for him?
questions.a: David prays that Yahweh not keep back his acts of mercy from David, but rather, let Yahweh’s covenant faithfulness and his trustworthiness always preserve David.

questions.q: What does David say is happening to him?
questions.a: Troubles that cannot be numbered surround him, and his iniquities have caught up with him so that he can no longer see clearly. They are more than the hairs on his head, and his heart has failed him.

questions.q: What does David pray that Yahweh will be pleased to do?
questions.a: He prays that Yahweh will be pleased to rescue him.

questions.q: What does David pray will happen to those who pursue his life?
questions.a: He prays that they have shame and be completely disappointed, and that they be turned back and brought to dishonor.

questions.q: What does David pray for those who seek Yahweh and love his salvation?
questions.a: He prays that they rejoice and be glad in Yahweh, and that they say continually, “May Yahweh be great.”

questions.q: How does David describe the Lord?
questions.a: The Lord thinks about him, is his help, and comes to David’s rescue.

commentary.text: Verses 1–5 Doubts and fears about the eternal state, are a horrible pit and miry clay, and have been so to many a dear child of God. There is power enough in God to help the weakest, and grace enough to help the unworthiest of all that trust in him. The psalmist waited patiently; he continued believing, hoping, and praying. This is applicable to Christ. His agony, in the garden and on the cross, was a horrible pit and miry clay. But those that wait patiently for God do not wait in vain. Those that have been under religious melancholy, and by the grace of God have been relieved, may apply ver. #(2) very feelingly to themselves; they are brought up out of a horrible pit. Christ is the Rock on which a poor soul can alone stand fast. Where God has given stedfast hope, he expects there should be a steady, regular walk and conduct. God filled the psalmist with joy, as well as peace in believing. Multitudes, by faith beholding the sufferings and glory of Christ, have learned to fear the justice and trust in the mercy of God through Him. Many are the benefits with which we are daily loaded, both by the providence and by the grace of God.

The psalmist foretells that work of wonder, redemption by our Lord Jesus Christ. The Substance must come, which is Christ, who must bring that glory to God, and that grace to man, which it was impossible the sacrifices should ever do. Observe the setting apart of our Lord Jesus to the work and office of Mediator. In the volume, or roll, of the book it was written of him. In the close rolls of the Divine decrees and counsel, the covenant of redemption was recorded. Also, in all the volumes of the Old Testament something was written of him, Joh 19:28. Now the purchase of our salvation is made, the proclamation is sent forth, calling us to come and accept it. It was preached freely and openly. Whoever undertook to preach the gospel of Christ, would be under great temptation to conceal it; but Christ, and those he calls to that work, are carried on in it. May we believe his testimony, trust his promise, and submit to his authority.

The best saints see themselves undone, unless continually preserved by the grace of God. But see the frightful view the psalmist had of sin. This made the discovery of a Redeemer so welcome. In all his reflections upon each step of his life, he discovered something amiss. The sight and sense of our sins in their own colours, must distract us, if we have not at the same time some sight of a Saviour. If Christ has triumphed over our spiritual enemies, then we, through him, shall be more than conquerors. This may encourage all that seek God and love his salvation, to rejoice in him, and to praise him. No griefs nor poverty can render those miserable who fear the Lord. Their God, and all that he has or does, is the ground of their joy. The prayer of faith can unlock his fulness, which is adapted to all their wants. The promises are sure, the moment of fulfilment hastens forward. He who once came in great humility, shall come again in glorious majesty.
